issues.legal_issue: A post-settlement grant of a fraction of a village within a permanently settled estate remains part of that estate and vests in the State when the estate is notified for abolition.
material_facts: The village was within a permanently settled estate.
A fraction of the village had been granted by the estate proprietor after permanent settlement.
The State notified the parent estate under the abolition legislation, and the notification included the fraction as part of the estate.
issues.conclusion: The fractional grant remained part of the estate and vested in the State when the parent estate was notified.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 1(3) and 1(4) and section 3(b) of the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948, the entire notified estate vests in the State. Section 2(8) of that Act recognizes a darmila inamdar as a landholder. The Court applied the understanding of ownership of a part of an estate in section 3(5) of the Madras Estates Land Act, 1908, as explained in Brahmayya v. Achiraju and Narayanaraju v. Suryanarayudu. A post-settlement grant of only part of a village does not thereby cease to be part of the parent estate.

rule.if: challenge_to_estate_notification and parent_estate_permanently_settled and fractional_post_settlement_grant_within_estate and parent_estate_notified

predicates.challenge_to_estate_notification: A proceeding challenges the inclusion or treatment of property in a notification abolishing an estate.
predicates.parent_estate_permanently_settled: The property lies within an estate that was permanently settled.
predicates.fractional_post_settlement_grant_within_: The estate proprietor granted a fraction of a village within the estate after permanent settlement.
predicates.parent_estate_notified: The State notified the parent estate under legislation providing for its abolition and vesting.

issues.definition: When a notification challenge concerns a fractional post-settlement grant within a permanently settled estate, and the parent estate has been notified, the fractional grant vests in the State.

issues.legal_issue: A post-settlement grant that gives its holder ownership of part of an estate is not protected as a right in land under the provision governing rights created by a landholder.
material_facts: The grant was a post-settlement minor inam of a fraction of a village within the estate.
The inamdar was a landholder because the grant made the inamdar an owner of part of the estate.
The parent estate was notified, and the inamdar argued that the grant was protected as a right created by a landholder.
issues.conclusion: The grant was not protected by section 20; the inam vested with the estate, leaving the inamdar entitled to claim compensation under the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3(b) and 3(c) distinguish ownership of an estate, which vests under section 3(b), from other rights in or over an estate, addressed by section 3(c). Section 20 protects rights created by a landholder, not ownership of an estate or a part of it. Its provisions concerning termination and compensation for the unexpired period of a right also indicate that it concerns limited rights rather than ownership. This reading accords with the Act’s purpose of abolishing intermediate tenures and establishing a direct relationship between the State and cultivators.

predicates.challenge_to_estate_notification: A proceeding challenges the treatment of a grant when the parent estate is notified for abolition.
predicates.fractional_grant_makes_holder_owner_of_e: The grant gives its holder ownership of a part of the estate.
predicates.grant_created_by_landholder: The grant was created by a person who held the estate as a landholder.

issues.definition: If a proceeding concerns a landholder-created grant that makes its holder an owner of part of an estate, the grant is not protected as a land right.

issues.legal_issue: A holder whose ownership of part of an estate vests in the State is entitled to claim a share of the compensation payable for the estate.
material_facts: The fractional inam formed part of the estate and vested in the State upon notification.
The legislation determined compensation for the estate as a whole, with the estate’s income including income from the inam lands.
The legislation provided for apportioning compensation among the principal landholder and other persons whose rights or interests in the estate vested in the State.
issues.conclusion: The inamdar was entitled to claim compensation for the transfer of the inam to the Government, although the compensation was determined for the estate as a whole.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 25, 27, 37 and 44 of the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948, provide for determining compensation for the estate as a whole, calculating it by reference to the estate’s income, and apportioning it among the principal landholder and other persons whose rights or interests vest in the Government. Section 45 concerns distribution of the principal landholder’s compensation for an impartible estate and does not extinguish the separate entitlement of other interest holders under section 44.

predicates.compensation_apportionment_under_estate_: A proceeding concerns compensation following the transfer of an estate to the State under an abolition scheme.
predicates.holder_owns_part_of_vested_estate: The holder owned part of the estate that transferred to the State.
predicates.estate_compensation_includes_part_income: The compensation calculation for the estate includes income attributable to the holder’s part.
predicates.compensation_apportioned_to_other_vested: The scheme provides for apportionment to persons other than the principal landholder whose interests in the estate transferred to the State.

issues.definition: When compensation is determined for a transferred estate using income that includes the holder’s part, and the scheme apportions compensation to other interest holders, the holder is entitled to claim compensation.
